agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now. All three suites pass: `node run-tests.js` (1 passing), the registered contract check `node checks/contract.cjs` (passed), and the new extended checks (passed). I left Amabie itself unconnected (`amabie setup` wasn't part of the task and would add hooks) and didn't touch `checks/contract.cjs` or `amabie.project.json`, so the registered proof hash stays valid.

## What was broken and what I changed

**`src/storage.js`** — `key()` was `id => id`, dropping the tenant entirely, so `('a','same')` and `('b','same')` collided. Replaced with a length-prefixed composite `` `${tenant.length}:${tenant}|${id.length}:${id}` ``, which is injective even when tenant/id contain `:`/`|` or look like each other's delimiters.

**`src/replay.js`** — replay filtered to `op:'put'` only, so `open(exportJournal())` silently resurrected deleted pairs. Now applies every event in order; `apply()` already handled both ops.

**`src/api.js`**
- The read cache was never invalidated — cached hits *and* cached misses went stale after any mutation. `apply()` now does `cache.delete(k)` for the affected key, so all mutation paths (put, remove, batch, replay) keep reads fresh, including after journal replay.
- `batch` ignored `event.op` (always `rows.set`, so batch deletes were no-ops) and bypassed `apply`. It now routes each event through `mutate({...e})`, giving in-order application, journal entries, and cache invalidation.
- `journal.push(...history.map(...))` replaced with a per-event loop (avoids spread's argument-count limit on long histories); detach-copy semantics unchanged.
- `exportJournal` already returned detached copies and is unchanged.

**`checks/extended-contract.cjs`** (new) — covers contract clauses the smoke check misses: delimiter/punctuation key collisions, cached-miss freshness via put/batch, cached-hit staleness via remove/batch-delete, batch call-order and last-write-wins, exportJournal detachment (tampering with the array and its objects leaks neither into state nor later exports), `open(exportJournal())` including deletions, history preserved for subsequent exports/mutations, and repeated-replay equivalence.
